{{Short description|On endomorphisms of Weyl algebras}}{{distinguish|text=the [[Uniformly bounded representation#Dixmier problem|Dixmier problem]] in representation theory}}
In [[algebra]], the '''Dixmier conjecture''', stated by [[Jacques Dixmier]] in 1968,<ref>{{Citation | last1=Dixmier | first1=Jacques | authorlink=Jacques Dixmier |title=Sur les algèbres de Weyl | url=http://www.numdam.org/item?id=BSMF_1968__96__209_0 | mr=0242897 | year=1968 | journal=Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France | volume=96 | pages=209–242 | doi=10.24033/bsmf.1667 | doi-access=free }} (problem 1)</ref> originally asked whether any [[endomorphism]] of the first [[Weyl algebra]] <math>A_1 </math> over a field of characteristic zero is an [[automorphism]]. The analogous statement for the <math>n</math>-th Weyl algebra <math>A_n </math> was recorded in 1982 by [[Hyman Bass|Bass]], Connell, and Wright, who attributed it to communications from [[Leonid Vaserstein]] and [[Victor Kac]],<ref name="BCW1982">{{cite journal|last1=Bass|first1=Hyman|last2=Connell|first2=Edwin H.|last3=Wright |first3=David |title=The Jacobian conjecture: Reduction of degree and formal expansion of the inverse|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |series=New Series |volume=7 |issue=2 |year=1982 |at=p. 297 |doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1982-15032-7|mr=0663785
|doi-access=free }}</ref> and was later referred to as the "generalized Dixmier conjecture".<ref name="vandenEssen1997">{{cite conference|last=van den Essen|first=Arno|title=Polynomial Automorphisms and the Jacobian Conjecture|book-title=Algèbre non commutative, groupes quantiques et invariants|conference=Septième Contact Franco-Belge, Reims, 26–30 June 1995|series=Séminaires et Congrès|volume=2 |publisher=Société Mathématique de France |location=Paris |year=1997 |at=p. 75, Conjecture 3.26 and Remark 3.27 |isbn=2-85629-052-3 |mr=1601194 |url=https://smf.emath.fr/publications/polynomial-automorphisms-and-jacobian-conjecture
}}</ref><ref name="Tsuchimoto2005"/>

[[Yoshifumi Tsuchimoto|Tsuchimoto]] in 2005,<ref name="Tsuchimoto2005">{{Citation | last1=Tsuchimoto | first1=Yoshifumi | title=Endomorphisms of Weyl algebra and p-curvatures | year=2005 | journal=Osaka J. Math.| volume=42 | pages=435–452}}</ref> and independently [[Belov-Kanel]] and [[Maxim Kontsevich|Kontsevich]] in 2007,<ref name="BKK">{{Citation | last1=Belov-Kanel | first1=Alexei | last2=Kontsevich | first2=Maxim | title=The Jacobian conjecture is stably equivalent to the Dixmier conjecture | arxiv=math/0512171 | mr=2337879 | year=2007 | journal=Moscow Mathematical Journal | volume=7 | issue=2 | pages=209–218| doi=10.17323/1609-4514-2007-7-2-209-218 | bibcode=2005math.....12171B | s2cid=15150838 }}</ref> showed that the Dixmier conjecture is stably equivalent to the Jacobian conjecture: the Dixmier conjecture for the ''n''-th Weyl algebra <math>A_n</math> implies the Jacobian conjecture for polynomial maps in ''n'' variables, while conversely the Jacobian conjecture in <math>2n</math> variables implies the Dixmier conjecture for <math>A_n</math>.<ref name="BKK"/> In July 2026, a counterexample to the [[Jacobian conjecture]] in three variables was found,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2580374-ais-solution-to-87-year-old-riddle-takes-mathematicians-by-surprise/|title=AI's solution to 87-year-old riddle takes mathematicians by surprise|author=Matthew Sparkes|date=July 20, 2026|publisher=[[New Scientist]]}}</ref> which by the first of these implications shows that the Dixmier conjecture is false for <math>A_n</math> for all <math>n \geq 3</math>.

The conjecture remains open for the first and second Weyl algebras, since the Jacobian conjecture is still open in two variables. The case of the first Weyl algebra <math>A_1</math> was the problem originally posed by Dixmier; a proposed proof of this case was announced by Alexander Zheglov in 2024.<ref>{{cite arXiv | last=Zheglov | first=Alexander | title=The Conjecture of Dixmier for the first Weyl algebra is true | year=2024 | eprint=2410.06959 | class=math.AG}}</ref>
